name: Zynga (Take-Two)
tagline: Free-to-play mobile games label powering half of Take-Two's bookings
facts: Not disclosed; tens of millions MAU (est.)

strategy.label: Mission
strategy.text: Connect the world through games: free-to-play titles monetised by in-app purchases and ads, never cash payouts.

strategy.label: Core strategy
strategy.text: Multi-studio portfolio (Peak, Rollic, Small Giant, StarLark, NaturalMotion) with relentless live ops on evergreen puzzle and casual hits.

strategy.label: Contrast to RMG
strategy.text: Players pay for fun (boosters, lives, virtual chips) but can never cash out, so not a money game under PROGA.

strategy.label: Moat
strategy.text: Live-ops expertise, Take-Two cross-promotion and ad network, data-driven UA at scale, Rollic hyper-casual funnel.

strategy.label: Key bet
strategy.text: Grow casual hits (Toon Blast, Match Factory!, Color Block Jam) and new launches like Top Goal, CSR 3.

strategy.label: Your view
strategy.text: Is Zynga Poker's virtual-chip social casino one regulator decision away from being treated like real-money gaming?

customers.pain: Want short relaxing sessions with a sense of progress
customers.why: Polished match/puzzle loops, daily events, fair free play, optional boosters

customers.pain: Want poker thrills without gambling money or legal risk
customers.why: Virtual chips, social tables, no cash-out keeps it entertainment

customers.who: Friends and families on Words With Friends
customers.pain: Want asynchronous play to stay connected
customers.why: Turn-based social play, long-lived friend graphs, brand familiarity

customers.pain: Want to progress faster and keep streaks
customers.why: Bundles, battle passes, events; fair value and limited-time offers

customers.who: App marketers and brands buying in-game ads
customers.pain: Need scaled mobile reach with measurable installs
customers.why: Huge casual audience, rewarded video, Take-Two/Zynga ad stack

rows.how: Boosters, lives, virtual chips, passes; items have no cash value
Rewarded video, interstitials, offerwalls via ad network
Virtual chip packs; winnings cannot be redeemed for money
Revenue share with IP owners; Star Wars Hunters shut Oct 2025

bullets.label: Revenue mix
bullets.text: Mostly IAP, with meaningful advertising; mobile was 49% of Take-Two FY26 bookings ($3.3B).

bullets.label: Users vs payers
bullets.text: Typically 2–5% of players pay (est.); whales fund free play for the rest.

bullets.label: Unit economics
bullets.text: LTV must beat CPI; long-lived live-ops titles amortise development, new launches carry high kill risk.

bullets.label: Growth levers
bullets.text: Live ops on evergreen hits, new launches, Rollic funnel, GTA VI (19 Nov 2026) halo for cross-promotion.

bullets.label: RMG lesson
bullets.text: No cash-out means no gambling classification: Zynga avoided India's ban that erased Dream11 and WinZO revenue.

friction: Paywalled difficulty spikes frustrate non-paying players
Frequent ads interrupt short casual sessions
Social casino can feel like gambling to regulators
Shutdowns like Star Wars Hunters strand paid purchases
Notification and offer overload drives uninstalls
